The template is `MATCH (p:SecretsIAMVaultPolicy {uid: row.vault_policy_uid}) MATCH (s:SecretsIAMSecretMetadataPath {uid: row.secret_path_uid}) MERGE (p)-[rel:SECRETS_IAM_GRANTS_SECRET_READ]->(s)`, and the token is static in the template (no %s: no value is ever encoded into a relationship type). The relationship MERGEs on its two endpoint nodes alone, so there is no identity block and no plain-string SET property that is stable offline: scope_id, generation_id, confidence, and evidence_fact_ids are per-run or data-carried values, evidence_source is the writer's stamp, and capabilities is a row-carried list the writer's unit test covers while lane 7 proves the capability gate by absence. Exactly three edges: lane A resolves an IRSA web-identity exact chain whose Vault role carries two token policies with one read rule each (grants-vault-policy-1 and grants-vault-policy-2 to their two secret paths) and lane B an EKS Pod Identity exact chain whose role carries one (grants-vault-policy-3 to its secret path), so both identity mechanisms prove the policy-to-path fan-out. The other six lanes contribute nothing on purpose -- lane C carries a full chain without any Vault role bound to its service account, the ghost role binds a service account nobody observed, lane D's wildcard web-identity subject never matches exactly, lane E's wildcard Vault bound-service-account selector refuses the exact join, lane F's Deny trust statement grants nothing, lane 7's list-only rule grants no read, and lane 8's read rule names a path with no KV metadata.
